- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in the following 3–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–7 days.  
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% gap) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, expect mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 7–14 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently lower than model (especially in first 10 days), model is overconfident; reduce first 5–10 days by 1–2% and adjust later days to follow true trend.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment turns bearish, forecast should slope downward).
